messages:
Maya Li: FYI — Velox Health (enterprise) just asked for a Dedicated pool commit sizing recommendation. They expect ~300 RPS of chat completions, average 3k tokens per session, p99 latency target <250ms, region: eu-west-2 only (data residency). Sales wants a 1-page commit recommendation and a monthly cost estimate they can sign to. Can we sketch numbers?

Jonah Park: Quick q: 300 RPS * 3k tokens = 900k tokens/sec? That math seems off. Are you doing sessions/sec vs requests/sec?

Maya Li: Good catch. They measure RPS as completion requests, not full session streams — average response length ~480 tokens, so about 300 * 480 = 144k tokens/sec sustained. Bursts ~2x during morning window.

Sanya Patel: Ok so sustained ~144k tok/s, burst up to 288k tok/s. Model mix? Velox said 70% on a quantized 13B for typical requests and 30% on a 70B variant for long-form summaries. We'll assume q13=13B q4f and q70=70B q4f.

Jonah Park: Rough per-GPU capacity (ballpark for our serving runtime):
```
- A100-80GB (13B q4f): ~8k tokens/sec per GPU
- H100-80GB or A100-80GB (70B q4f): ~18k tokens/sec per GPU
```
Those are conservative with batch & prefix caching.

Maya Li: Using that: sustained GPUs needed = ceil((144k * (0.7/8k + 0.3/18k))) — but easier to split by model class.

Jonah Park: Split calc:
```
13B load = 144k * 0.7 = 100.8k tok/s -> 100.8k / 8k ≈ 12.6 -> 13 GPUs (A100)
70B load = 144k * 0.3 = 43.2k tok/s -> 43.2k / 18k ≈ 2.4 -> 3 GPUs (H100)
Sustained floor ≈ 16 GPUs total
Burst buffer (2x for peak) -> target pool = 32 GPUs total
Add safety buffer (1.1x) -> ~35 GPUs
```

Sanya Patel: For commits we usually size toward steady-state plus a ~30% buffer not full burst. Sales prefers a predictable monthly commit and use burst capacity for spikes. So propose commit = sustained * 1.3 -> 16 * 1.3 ≈ 21 GPUs (round up), and allow autoscale for bursts up to 35 with overage billing.

Luis Ortega: Need to call out GPU flavors and regional availability — eu-west-2 has limited H100 capacity and H100 SKUs cost ~40-50% more. Another option: use more A100s for the 70B but performance drops; we could use model distillation or a 30B mid-tier to reduce H100 need.

Maya Li: Sales constraint: customer asked for single commit line (no mixing flavors). They prefer single SKU commit for procurement simplicity. If so, must convert to an equivalent A100 commit. Can someone run a quick equivalence?

Jonah Park: Equivalent A100 estimate for 70B: one H100 ≈ 1.9 A100 for our runtime on 70B. So 3 H100 ≈ 6 A100. Total A100-equivalent = 13 (13B GPUs) + 6 = 19 A100. Round to commit = 21 A100 (with 1.3x steady buffer). Bursts handled by ephemeral H100s if available or on-demand A100s.

Sanya Patel: Cost roughing (using committed monthly effective rates):
```
assume A100 reserved effective rate = $2.8 / GPU-hour
hours/month = 720
commit 21 A100 -> monthly = 21 * 720 * 2.8 ≈ $42,336
on-demand burst cap (ephemeral) assume 14 GPUs * 720 * 4.5 ≈ $45,360 if fully used (but usually much less)
Estimated total expected spend with commit offsetting base = ~$45k-$60k/mo depending on burst patterns
```

Jonah Park: Note: those numbers include only compute — add storage, egress, and support margins (~15%). So quote to sales should show compute + 15% ops + 10% margin.

Maya Li: Action items: Jonah run a small stress test in eu-west-2 to validate tokens/sec per GPU for our latest runtime artifacts (use real config: batch=64, dynamic kv cache, seq len=1024). Sanya draft commit recommendation doc (1-pager) with the A100-equivalent approach and explicit burst policy. Luis confirm H100 availability and an alternate SKU plan.

Luis Ortega: Will check capacity with cloud partner and confirm spot/ephemeral options. If H100 are tight we propose hybrid: commit 21 A100 and allow 4 H100 on-demand for peak 70B jobs.

infra-bot: Runbook: Dedicated commit sizing checklist -> https://redwood.internal/runbooks/dedicated-commit-sizing (added by infra-bot) :white_check_mark:

Sanya Patel: I'll put the doc in /shared/sales/velox-health/ and ping @sales to prep contract language.

Maya Li: Thanks all. If tests show per-GPU throughput >= our conservative numbers we can lower commit to 18 A100 and accept slightly higher overage risk. Will update once Jonah posts test results. :thumbsup:
